verdict.rationale: mise records per-project tool version requests in a checked-in mise.toml, and `--pin` writes the exact resolved version. It switches to those versions automatically by directory, and a committed lockfile with `mise install --locked` makes every install use the same versions. A community user independently says it supports pinning exact versions of many languages. Missing for 10: detailed documentation or hands-on evidence of how `--locked` enforces pins when they drift (e.g., failure behavior on mismatch).

support.subject: As a developer, I can pin exact versions of packages and tools per project and have the manager respect those pins

citations.quote: Keep multiple versions of Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, and other tools on the same machine, then declare which ones a project uses in `mise.toml`.
Add `--pin` to write the resolved version instead
Once activated, mise can automatically switch between different versions of tools based on the directory you're in.
Commit a lockfile and install with `mise install --locked`. Every job then installs the same versions
It supports pinning exact versions of many more languages than devenv does.
